transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-03-16
- Time: 14:00 PT
- Duration: 54 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (SableWorks Head of ML), Aaron Lim (Platform Eng), Caroline Zhou (Finance)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style pulse on usage/costs and a concrete pilot kickoff to validate latency and cost levers. Discussed dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, KV/prefix caching, quantization options, and SOC2/KMS requirements. Agreed to an initial 4-week pilot with guardrails and a benchmark run.

[00:00] Maya Chen: all right everyone thanks for joining — we'll kick off, um — this is the SableWorks runway health pulse and then pivot into the pilot kickoff. Diego and I will lead.
[00:18] Priya Nair: hi thanks — excited, we just want to make sure performance and cost look good before we expand beyond the current sandbox.
[00:28] Diego Alvarez: cool, quick agenda — current utilization, cost drivers, reliability incidents, then pilot scope. Also quick security tick box.
[00:45] Aaron Lim: just to flag, last week we had two p95 spikes during batch jobs at 03:00, and we lost a small percentage of requests when a rollout bumped a node pool. Not a major user impact but it showed brittle autoscale.
[01:12] Maya Chen: thanks, good callout. That sounds like a routing/autoscaler timing window; we usually recommend a small buffer capacity and can enable fallback to a cheaper model variant during node transitions.
[01:34] Priya Nair: question — how intrusive is prefix/KV cache to our prompt pipeline? We do a lot of short-turn conversational prompts with some sticky context.
[01:48] Diego Alvarez: for short-turn chat, KV caching is low-friction — it caches key/value past tokens so subsequent requests skip recomputation. There can be memory tuning; on Redwood Dedicated we can size cache per tenant. On hosted, there's an automated LRU but we can suggest config.
[02:10] Priya Nair: ok, cost — Caroline, can you remind the monthly run rate we saw last quarter?
[02:18] Caroline Zhou: sure, rough numbers — about $42k monthly, spike to $58k in January when we did the product demo traffic. Majority of cost from long-context summarization jobs and fine-grain embeddings.
[02:38] Maya Chen: thanks. Main levers we discussed historically are: quantization (reduce per-token compute), batching windows (when latency tolerant), and model routing (cheaper variant for low-importance traffic). Diego, can you run the numbers briefly?
[02:55] Diego Alvarez: yeah, rough math on the call — if we Q4-quantize to 4-bit where it preserves quality for your summarization prompts, we estimate 20–30% GPU cost down. Batching for the summarization pipeline could further drop token compute by 15% if you accept 200–300ms extra latency. For embeddings we recommended cache of 24 hours and approximate dedupe to avoid repeated calls.
[03:26] Aaron Lim: embedding cache sounds great — what's the retention/consistency tradeoff? We have semantic hashing and sometimes update vectors.
[03:36] Diego Alvarez: you can evict on update events; many teams use a short TTL (1–6 hours) for high-change sets, longer for static indexes. Redwood's cache supports TTL and explicit invalidation hooks.
[03:54] Priya Nair: reliability — can you explain the automated fallbacks you mentioned? During the spike, we didn't want to lose responses.
[04:03] Maya Chen: fallback policies let traffic route to a compatible model variant (e.g., smaller LLamaX-style model) when a primary cluster is at capacity. It preserves throughput and degrades quality gracefully. We can attach per-route SLOs and circuit-breaker thresholds.
[04:22] Aaron Lim: do you support pinned versions? We sometimes need a freeze for compliance.
[04:27] Diego Alvarez: yes, pin model versions and rollouts with canary. That's part of the rollout UI — you get tracing at token level and you can auto rollback.
[04:40] Caroline Zhou: security check — we need SOC2 and KMS integration for the pilot. Also SSO and RBAC for console access.
[04:49] Maya Chen: yes, we've shared SOC2 previously but we'll resend the one-pager and a KMS integration guide. On SSO — SAML is supported, RBAC is role-based, and audit logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[05:05] Priya Nair: great. Pilot scope — what are the measurable success criteria?
[05:10] Diego Alvarez: propose: 4-week pilot, target p95 latency for chat < 320ms for production-like traffic, token cost reduction of 20% or more vs current baseline, no more than 0.5% error/failure rate during business hours. We'll run an initial benchmark and then a 2-week live run.
[05:29] Priya Nair: that sounds reasonable. We also want to validate model output quality for our summarization workflows — could we lock a prompt set?
[05:38] Maya Chen: absolutely; please share your top 50 prompts and example expected outputs. We'll run evals and produce a quality delta report for each quant/model variant.
[05:52] Aaron Lim: infra wise, we prefer VPC peering for pilot, not on-prem yet. Can Redwood do VPC + private endpoints?
[06:00] Diego Alvarez: yes — Redwood Private supports a VPC connector; we can provision a private endpoint and you can bring your KMS. For the pilot we can do a scoped VPC peered setup or dedicated capacity if you want isolation.
[06:13] Caroline Zhou: cost model question — pilot will be approved faster if we do metered usage vs commit. Any downside?
[06:21] Maya Chen: metered buys flexibility but may have higher unit cost. If you expect stable traffic, a short reserved commit for the pilot can lower unit price and guarantee headroom. We'll show both numbers in the pricing sheet.
[06:36] Priya Nair: competitor check — we eval'd Anthropic last quarter but the latency profile there didn't match our p95 needs. Vertex AI was cheaper for embeddings but integration work was heavier.
[06:49] Diego Alvarez: understood. We'll highlight the routing/fallback + KV caching differentiator in the pilot writeup.
[06:58] Maya Chen: ok let's recap logistics and owners — Diego will prepare the benchmark config and expected SLO doc; Priya share prompt set and traffic profile; Caroline confirm budget mechanism. We'll aim to have the pilot kick-off runbook call week of 3/22.
[07:15] Priya Nair: quick question — for the quantization tests, do you need model-retraining or is it inference-only?
[07:22] Diego Alvarez: inference-only quantization paths for most open models — we recommend evaluation for output drift. If you need finetune-level quality, that would be separate.
[07:34] Aaron Lim: during the live run, what visibility do we get into token-level cost?
[07:40] Maya Chen: Console shows per-route token breakdowns, per-model cost and p95 latency. We'll give a shared dashboard for the pilot with read-only links for your stakeholders.
[07:52] Caroline Zhou: sounds good. Also please include an estimated uplift in ops work during the pilot — we need to staff an on-call.
[07:59] Maya Chen: we'll include an ops runbook and recommended on-call schedule. Diego, any other technical notes?
[08:07] Diego Alvarez: one more: during the benchmark we'll simulate a rollout-induced node churn to validate fallback behavior — it's low-risk but catches the autoscaler issue Aaron mentioned.
[08:20] Priya Nair: perfect.

Recap & Close:
- Pilot: 4 weeks; kickoff runbook call targeted week of 2027-03-22.
- Success criteria: p95 < 320ms, >=20% token cost reduction, <0.5% error rate.
- Deliverables: benchmark config, prompt set evals, security doc + KMS guide, pricing options (metered vs short commit).

Final remarks: everyone agreed on next steps. Maya thanked the SableWorks team and closed meeting at 14:54 PT.
